product.name: Atuin Desktop
product.one_liner: Turn your team's shell scripts and runbooks into executable, version-controlled docs that stay current because they actually run.
features: Executable runbook blocks: mix shell commands, SQL queries, HTTP calls, and live Prometheus charts in a single document that runs top-to-bottom
Serial run-all with pause blocks: click Play to execute multi-step deploys sequentially, with human-confirmation checkpoints before destructive steps
Atuin Hub team sync: share shell history and runbooks across the org with per-user and per-team granular permissions, backed by end-to-end encryption
Jinja-style templating with shell history autocomplete: parameterize runbooks using variables, with autocomplete drawn from your team's real command history
Git-native CRDT workspaces: local-first, offline-capable co-editing that commits to Git — runbooks live in version control alongside the code they operate on

pain_to_feature_map.runbook_sprawl: Git-native CRDT workspaces: one canonical, version-controlled location per runbook — no more Confluence page vs. Notion doc vs. Slack thread debate
pain_to_feature_map.deploy_chaos: Serial run-all with pause blocks: reproducible deploy sequences with mandatory human checkpoints replace ad-hoc copy-paste from Slack
pain_to_feature_map.onboarding_debt: Executable getting-started runbooks: new engineers run their first deploy on day one from a document that autocompletes from real team command history
pain_to_feature_map.script_rot: Executable blocks ensure documentation is always tested — a runbook that hasn't run recently fails loudly, making rot visible before incidents expose it
pain_to_feature_map.shell_history_not_shared: Atuin Hub team sync: every engineer's shell history is searchable by the team, surfacing the five commands that only one person knew

stack_signals: Kubernetes or ECS for container orchestration
PostgreSQL or MySQL with manual migration runbooks
GitHub Actions or CircleCI CI/CD pipelines
AWS, GCP, or Azure with multiple environments (staging, prod)
Bash and Python scripts owned by the platform or infra team
pain_keywords: who knows how to restart X
five commands only one person knows
anti_signals: No-code or low-code teams with no terminal ownership
Pure SaaS teams with zero infra footprint (PaaS-only, Heroku-button deploys)
Large enterprises with dedicated change-management and ITSM ticketing (ServiceNow gates every deploy)
Teams where all operational runbooks are already fully automated in CI/CD with zero manual steps
role_targets: DevOps / Infrastructure engineer (primary buyer and champion)
Platform engineer or SRE (day-to-day user, defines runbook standards)
Backend engineering lead (approves tooling, feels onboarding pain directly)
Engineering manager (budget holder, cares about MTTR and onboarding ramp)
icp.company_stage: Seed through Series C; sweet spot is Series A–B scale-ups growing from 15 to 75 engineers where tribal knowledge debt is compounding faster than the team can document it

tone_rules: Lead with the operational pain, never the feature — open with 'the five commands only one person knows' not 'our runbook editor'
Use their exact vocabulary: runbooks, playbooks, scripts, commands, deploys — never 'workflows', 'automations', or 'empowering your team'
Be concrete and specific — name the tool they're replacing (Confluence, Notion, Slack threads), not a generic 'documentation solution'
Developer-register: direct, no fluff, no buzzwords — write like a senior infra engineer Slacking a teammate, not a SaaS landing page
Respect their time: cold outreach subject lines under 8 words, body copy under 80 words, one ask per message

competitors.Confluence: Passive document store — pages go stale the day they're written, there is no execution layer, and search surfaces the wrong version during an incident at 2 AM
competitors.Notion: Beautiful but inert — you cannot run a database migration or a rolling deploy from a Notion page; it is a whiteboard, not an operator
competitors.internal wikis: Zero accountability, no execution, and rot by design — nobody owns staleness, nobody is paged when a command no longer works, tribal knowledge migrates back to Slack within weeks
competitors.Retool runbooks: Requires admin setup and a BI or ops-tools team to maintain; built for business operations workflows not terminal-native infra tasks; engineers don't live in it
